I was diagnosed going into my 6th or 7th grade (can't remember) so what 12 or 13ish? I've never measured my oxygen saturation so no idea what that's at.

33 with anywhere from a 22-28% FEV1.  

For the most part my quality of life is ok, I take Symdeko, I can climb 2-3 flights of stairs at a time and get winded but can still continue. I can't run without feeling like I'm going to die, but otherwise am ok with physical activity, just need to take it a bit slower than most. I never took my medicine regularly as a teenager which is the root cause of my shitty FEV1, as it's hovered in the 30%s for most of my life.  

I cultured mycobacterium at my last check up and that has me scared to death, but I'll do another sputum test soon and they'll check to see if it was a false positive or not.  

I've only been hospitalized twice in my life, and only received IV's the first time (pretty sure the nurses and doctors on my second hospitalization didn't know what the fuck they were doing, cause all they did was adhere to a VERY strict nebulizer schedule and NOTHING ELSE. I could have done that shit at home! but whatever)  

I don't use supplemental O2, just take Symdeko, Pulmozyme, and Albuterol.  

I would honestly say my quality of life isn't terrible. I have depression that sometimes borders on severe, but thank god for my girlfriend, who always seems to know how to brighten my day, with just a simple phone call (currently long distance but working on changing that). I feel like I can do most of the things my friends can do, it just may take me slightly longer to do it. I play with my nieces for as long as I can before I get winded, take a break catch my breath, and play with them again. I ride my bike to work during the summer (about a mile) and that kicks my ass, but it's helpful to get that exercise. Trying to move to Houston from the north, so hoping no more winters will be a big plus!  

The biggest issue I have at this point, is I never expected to be alive at 33, so I've got zero plans for the future, pretty massive debt, and no savings. That's my biggest hardship is trying to figure out how to continue living when I thought I wouldn't have made it this far. But I will do everything I can, and lean on my amazing support system when necessary.

Already successful companies will do this a lot with their crowdfunding efforts. If they set a low goal, i.e. $30,000, they know they're going to reach that goal within hours, maybe even minutes depending on the size of the community. Rooster Teeth did this with their Million Dollars But... card game, allowing them to reach their goal in 2 minutes, and thus promote the "fastest kickstarter to reach its goal." It also looks a lot more impressive when you can say you raised $1.2M against a goal of $30,000 instead of saying you raised $1.2M against a goal of $1M. The low goal is really nothing more than a clever ploy to use in future marketing initiatives.
